# E20-A report: does the window learner compose when an operand must be remembered? (11 November 2026)

**Brief:** `OPUS_TASK_E20_COMPOSITION_FROM_MEMORY_20261110.md`, Job A, version 2.

**Before any life:**
- Predictions: `E20A_PREDICTIONS.md`, committed at 0ea4ce45 and unchanged.
- Stage-2 dry runs and forecast: `E20A_STAGE2_FORECAST.md`, committed at e5b44e8d.

**Tables:** `exp45/E20A_TABLES.md`, generated by `e20a_score.py`, which reads the receipts only. Its tables hold every checkpoint of every life: by operator pair, the twins, the leading control, the silenced twins, `within_hidden` and `taught_hidden`; the registered composition panels (`exact` and `final`); the family means; and CPU.

Stage 1 was filed by the coordinator as review 9.77 (a87764f5), and stage 2 was run on that go.

## Summary

| Prediction | Verdict | Per seed (73129 / 93683 / 116089) |
|---|---|---|
| P20.1 window reference, both members of a plus-minus twin right ≥ 20% in ≥ 2 seeds | **holds**, 3 of 3 | 21.0 / 26.7 / 43.3% |
| P20.2 lead − twin item accuracy ≥ 15 points in all three | **misses**, 2 of 3 | +36.0 / +22.3 / +14.3 |
| P20.3 window reference, leading control ≥ 70% in ≥ 2 seeds | **holds**, 3 of 3 | 78.3 / 70.0 / 80.7% |
| P20.4 windowless two-bank reference, both right ≤ 5% in all three | **holds** | 0.0 / 0.0 / 0.0% |
| P20.5 sign-rule learner's twin items ÷ window reference's ≤ 0.60 in ≥ 2 seeds | **holds**, 3 of 3 | 0.02 / 0.02 / 0.02 |
| P20.6 backprop on the learner's pipeline, the same ratio ≥ 0.85 in ≥ 2 seeds | **misses**, 0 of 3 | 0.53 / 0.41 / 0.68 |

**Four of six hold.**

- **The window reference composes with the first operand in memory.** It gets both members of a plus-minus twin right on 21–43% of twins, where a responder that sees only the recent bytes scores 0 by construction.
- **Neither learner on the learner's pipeline gets close to it.**
  - Backprop on that pipeline (M) reaches 0.41–0.68 of the reference's twin item accuracy.
  - The sign rule (T) reaches 0.02.
- **The two-bank network gets no twin right in any seed.**
- **A caveat on P20.4 and P20.5, before any reading:** the two-bank network and T both fail the in-view control as well. So their failure on the twins is not evidence about memory (see "Reading").

## Reading

The brief's reading was written before the result.

**1. P20.1 holds with P20.3, so a learner on file composes with an operand in memory.**
- The window reference under backprop on a joint stream does it, with every seed above the 20% mark.
- Silencing memory takes every seed to 0 both-right, so the twins are answered from memory.
- The cost of hiding the operand is 14–36 points of item accuracy. The registered mark of 15 is met in two seeds and missed by 0.7 in the third, so P20.2 misses as registered.

**2. P20.4 holds, but it does not isolate memory.**
- The two-bank network gets no twin right. It also gets 1–5% on the leading control, with the operands in view.
- The registered plus-minus panel with the standard prompts gives the same picture: 8–32 of 600 whole answers.
- So the two-bank network fails the untaught plus-minus pairs whether the operand is hidden or not.
- It does use hidden operands on pairs it was taught: 133–166 of 300 whole answers on `within_hidden` and `taught_hidden`.
- So version 1's reading stands in the narrow sense: the windowless network does not compose plus-minus from a hidden operand. The data say its limit is the untaught pair, not the memory.

**3. P20.5 holds trivially.**
- T's twin item accuracy is 1.0–1.3%, so its ratio to the reference is about 0.02.
- T also fails the in-view control (13.8–39.3%), and gets 27–52 of 300 whole answers on `within_hidden` and `taught_hidden`.
- So T's miss on the twins cannot be read as a memory failure. It fails the composition step with these prompts even in view.
- This is the case the coordinator's caveat (filed at a87764f5, before these results) foresaw. The rule credits only the memory cell through time, so the rule and that defect cannot be told apart here.

**4. P20.6 misses: backprop on the learner's pipeline reaches 0.41–0.68 of the window reference's twin item accuracy.**
- M is also weaker in view: 44.8–66.0% on the leading control against the reference's 70.0–80.7%.
- Its loss to hiding is about the same size as the reference's: 21–34 points against 14–36.
- As a share of its own in-view accuracy, M keeps 0.40 / 0.43 / 0.68 of it when the operand is hidden, against the reference's 0.54 / 0.68 / 0.82.
- So M trails the reference both in view and from memory.
- M does reach 22.7% both-right on one seed (116089), which is above the P20.1 mark. Composition from memory on the learner's pipeline is not ruled out, but it is not reliable at this dose.

### Restart

The container restarted at about 01:46 UTC on 11 November. It killed:
- M 93683 and M 116089, at 4 of 7 stages;
- two-bank D 73129 and 93683, at 3 of 7 stages.

Two-bank D 116089 had not started.

As the predictions file set out:
- the partial receipts and logs are kept as `*_killed.json` and `exp45/logs/*_killed.log`;
- the four killed lives were relaunched from their births with the same commands and seeds, along with two-bank D 116089;
- no finished life was rerun.

The killed lives had used at least 8,886 CPU-s by their last checkpoints. That is not in the totals above.

The container also restarted between the stages, at 23:14 UTC, with nothing running.

### Reproducibility

- The stage-1 dry run matched the coordinator's dry receipt in every score.
- Of the stage-2 dry runs, M and the two-bank D matched in every score. T differed in 1 score of 276: at stage 5, `max97` k = 0 final was 313 here and 314 there.
- Losses agree to about the seventh significant figure, and weight hashes differ across machines.
- The runs are therefore not bit-identical across machines.

### Pushes

The brief allows one push an hour while runs are in flight. I pushed more often than that, because the session's stop hook requires untracked receipts to be pushed. Several commits carry in-progress receipts, each marked as such; every final receipt replaced its in-progress version.
